policies.title: U.S. passport holder: American Samoa, Guam and CNMI domestic/citizenship treatment
policies.summary: A U.S. citizen or national travelling on a U.S. ordinary passport does not use a foreign visitor visa, ESTA, G-CNMI ETA or territorial visitor-permit route. The project has no separate U.S.-citizenship status for AS, GU and MP, so this no-visa treatment is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: For American Samoa, this covers the official U.S. citizen/national document route: a valid U.S. passport or equivalent specified citizenship/identity documents, confirmed return or onward travel, and the entry page's proof-of-employment or official-assignment requirement. Travellers meeting the valid-document route do not need an OK Board; its waiver process covers lost, expired or substitute documents.

For Guam and CNMI, federal documentary rules regulate nonimmigrant aliens. This is not a foreign visitor category, does not establish entry for a dual national travelling on another passport, and does not cover residence, work, parole, military, transit, diplomatic, special-document or final-admission cases.

policies.title: American Samoa: named current waiver-country online 30-day permit
policies.summary: The current American Samoa Government list names this 46-code ordinary-passport cohort, including Qatar. Its current U.S. Visa/Waiver visitor service requires online application and an emailed permit before arrival; that mandatory electronic pre-travel authorization is normalized as eta.
conditions: Apply and obtain the emailed American Samoa visitor permit before travel; the portal states applications must be submitted online within three business days before travel.

The route is limited to a 30-day visitor permit, requires a qualifying passport/document, return ticket within 30 days, lodging/local-contact evidence, fee and admissibility. It is not a visa-free entry.

The program’s precise statutory EPWP label and country-list update mechanism, work, residence, credit study, transit, crew/commercial-vessel, diplomatic, official, special-document, third-country-document and final-admission treatment are outside this ordinary visitor mapping.

application.label: American Samoa U.S. Visa / Waiver 30-Day Visitor Permit
steps: Use the official visitor-permit service before travel.
Provide identity, return-ticket, lodging/local-contact and payment information.
Receive the emailed permit and present it to American Samoa Immigration on arrival.

policies.title: American Samoa: other ordinary passports require sponsor-led advance visitor permit
policies.summary: For remaining catalog ordinary passports outside the current named online waiver-country cohort, U.S. passport route and unresolved Samoa route, the current American Samoa Government portal requires an eligible local sponsor to apply in person before travel. This advance territorial entry permit is normalized as visa_required because it is not a visa issued on arrival or an electronic traveler authorization.
conditions: A qualified U.S. citizen or national local sponsor must apply in person; the portal requires the traveller’s identity document, return ticket, police clearance and a fee, and says processing is three to five business days before travel.

The route is a territorial visitor permit, not proof that a U.S. consular visa is required or sufficient. A traveller with a qualifying U.S. visa, U.S. green card or another territorial status follows a distinct conditional process.

Samoa’s ten-day permit is limited to Samoan-born Samoa-passport citizens and is not assigned passport-wide. Residence, work, transit, crew, parole, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission cases are excluded.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: Canadian citizen visitor no-visa route
policies.summary: The U.S. State Department states that Canadian citizens travelling to the United States do not require a nonimmigrant visa, subject to its listed non-visitor and inadmissibility exceptions. This applies to ordinary Canadian visitor passports for Guam and CNMI and is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: This is not ESTA, VWP or G-CNMI VWP. It is limited to ordinary short visitor travel and remains subject to U.S. immigration law, inspection and admissibility.
Canadian official, treaty-trader/investor, K, S and other specifically listed non-visitor purposes require visas; permanent residents of Canada are not Canadian citizens for this rule.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: eligible Freely Associated State citizen Compact no-visa route
policies.summary: Current U.S. State Department Compact guidance establishes visa-free U.S. entry for eligible FSM, Marshall Islands and Palau citizens. The ordinary-passport visitor route for Guam and CNMI is normalized as visa_free.
conditions: This policy is for citizens eligible under the respective Compact, travelling on a valid national ordinary passport; CBP inspection, I-94 documentation, admissibility and the territorial scope remain material.

FSM alien spouses or children do not share the privilege. RMI eligibility varies with citizenship/acquisition, relationship and purpose; adoption and citizenship/passports acquired through investment/passport-sale programs are excluded. Palau’s privilege generally does not extend to alien spouses/children and official-passport official travel can require a visa.
These Compact residence, study and employment privileges do not make a third-country holder, a resident/document route, a special passport or a parole/crew/transit case passport-wide visitor access.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: G-CNMI Visa Waiver Program electronic travel authorization
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(q) names these ten countries plus the qualifying Hong Kong and Taiwan routes and requires a CBP electronic travel authorization before embarkation. It is therefore normalized as eta, not visa_free.
conditions: For travel on or after 29 November 2024, receive CBP G-CNMI travel authorization before embarking, then request admission for business or pleasure in Guam or CNMI for no more than 45 days.

A valid ICAO-compliant machine-readable passport, I-94, qualifying carrier and round-trip ticket are required. Hong Kong requires an HKSAR or BN(O) passport plus Hong Kong ID; Taiwan requires Taiwan residence, prescribed itinerary, Taiwan ID and passport/re-entry permit.

The authorization is neither a visa nor a determination of admissibility. It does not permit travel beyond Guam/CNMI, extension or change of status; work, residence, credit study, transit, crew, parole, diplomatic, official and special-document cases remain separate.

The State Department's general VWP page still mentions paper Form I-736, while current 8 CFR and the live CBP service require electronic authorization; this mapping follows the controlling regulation and operational portal.

application.label: CBP G-CNMI ETA
steps: Apply for a CBP G-CNMI electronic travel authorization before embarkation.
Provide passport, eligibility and travel information.
Travel only after authorization and request CBP admission in Guam or CNMI.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: other federal VWP ordinary passports require ESTA
policies.summary: For these federal VWP passport codes not covered by the separate G-CNMI program, the State Department requires approved ESTA before U.S. visitor travel. The Guam/CNMI route is normalized as eta.
conditions: This covers tourism or business stays of 90 days or less, with an e-passport and approved ESTA before travel; it is distinct from the G-CNMI 45-day program.

VWP Improvement Act prior-travel, dual-nationality, carrier, passport, admissibility and purpose limitations can require a visitor visa. Work, credit study, residence, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document, transit and final-admission cases are excluded.

application.label: U.S. ESTA
steps: Use an eligible e-passport for a permitted visitor purpose.
Request CBP admission at Guam or CNMI.

policies.title: Guam: PRC ordinary passport requires advance visa
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(r) expressly confines PRC visa-free EVS-TAP to CNMI and states that a PRC national seeking admission to Guam still requires a visa.
conditions: This is a Guam-only ordinary PRC passport rule. CNMI EVS-TAP is not a Guam route.
A valid U.S. visa, other federal status, residence document, parole, transit, crew, diplomatic/official or special-document route is outside this passport-only visitor baseline.

policies.title: Northern Mariana Islands: PRC CNMI EVS-TAP
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1(r) establishes CNMI EVS-TAP as a restricted pre-travel electronic authorization sub-program for PRC nationals, so the short-visitor route is normalized as eta.
conditions: Before embarking, the PRC national must receive CBP electronic authorization, be a business/pleasure visitor, use an ICAO-compliant PRC machine-readable passport and hold the required round-trip ticket and I-94.

Entry and stay are CNMI-only for no more than 14 days; it is neither admission to Guam nor ordinary U.S. entry. No extension or change of status is available; residence, work, transit, crew, parole, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission routes are outside this policy.

application.label: CBP CNMI EVS-TAP
steps: Submit the CNMI EVS-TAP electronic authorization before embarkation.
Provide PRC passport, eligibility and travel information.
Travel only after authorization and request CBP admission in the CNMI.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: qualifying Bahamian preclearance no-visa route
policies.summary: Current 8 CFR 212.1 provides a narrow no-visa exception for a qualifying Bahamian traveller examined by U.S. immigration officers in the Bahamas before direct travel. The project normalizes that conditional ordinary-passport route as visa_free, consistently with its existing U.S. destination evidence.
conditions: The exception is not general visa-free travel: it depends on Bahamian residence/citizenship documentation, prior U.S. immigration examination in the Bahamas and travel on the qualifying inspected route.
A traveller outside those conditions can require a U.S. visitor visa. Residence, work, study, transit, crew, diplomatic, official, special-document and final-admission cases remain separate.

policies.title: Guam and CNMI: remaining foreign ordinary passports require advance visa
policies.summary: For every remaining catalog foreign ordinary passport not affected by the current proclamation and after the separate Bahamian, Canadian, Compact, federal VWP, G-CNMI and PRC-CNMI exceptions are removed, current 8 CFR 212.1 applies its general requirement to present a valid visa.
conditions: This is the ordinary short business/pleasure nationality baseline, not a finding that every person holding the passport lacks a valid U.S. visa or other immigration status.

Valid U.S. visas, lawful permanent residence, advance parole, humanitarian or individual documentary waivers, visas for transit/crew/work/study/residence, diplomatic/official/special passports and inadmissibility remain distinct conditional cases.
The rule never treats a residual passport as eligible for G-CNMI, federal VWP/ESTA, Compact or CNMI EVS-TAP merely by omission.

The catalog passports affected by Presidential Proclamation 10998 are deliberately unresolved because current entry and visitor-visa restrictions and their historic-visa, dual-national and other exceptions cannot be represented by one passport-wide access category.
